blocks.value: Relational operators compare two operands and return a boolean (true/false) result.

Operator  Meaning           Example (x=11,y=3)  Result
>         Greater than      x > y               true
>=        Greater or equal  x >= y              true
<         Less than         x < y               false
<=        Less or equal     x <= y              false
==        Equal             x == y              false
!=        Not equal         x != y              true
A relational expression's result can be assigned straight to a boolean variable: boolean b = 10 > 2; assigns true.
Logical operators combine boolean expressions and are evaluated left to right.

Operator  Meaning                                    Example (A=true,B=false)  Result
&&        AND - true only if both operands are true   A && B                    false
||        OR - true if at least one operand is true    A || B                    true
^         XOR - true if exactly one operand is true    A ^ B                     true
!         NOT - reverses the operand's value           !A                        false
